items.question: What engine powers the AW189?
items.explanation: The AW189 is powered by two GE CT7-2E1 turboshaft engines.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Power Plant Limitations

items.question: With all engines operating and airspeed below 90 KIAS, what is the maximum continuous Power Index (PI)?
items.explanation: Maximum continuous PI with AEO below 90 KIAS is 100%; the 30-minute/5-minute range extends to 116%, with a 5-second transient limit of 123%.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Power Index Indicator (PI%)

items.question: One engine inoperative (OEI), what is the maximum PI for the 2.5-minute rating, and how long may PI exceed 164%?
options: 143–172%, no more than 30 seconds cumulative above 164%
items.explanation: OEI 2.5-minute range is 143–172% TQ, with automatic power reduction to 164% after 30 seconds cumulative time above 164%.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Power Index Indicator (PI%), OEI

items.question: What is the maximum gas generator speed (NG) transient limit, all engines operating?
items.explanation: AEO maximum continuous NG is 102.7%, with a 12-second transient limit of 103.2%.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Gas Generator Speed (NG%)

items.question: What is the maximum NG during a 2.5-minute OEI rating?
items.explanation: OEI NG 2.5-minute range extends from 102.8% up to a maximum of 105.0%.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Gas Generator Speed (NG%), OEI

items.question: What is the maximum ITT permitted during engine starting?
items.explanation: Maximum ITT for starting is 964°C.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Inter Turbine Temperature (ITT°C)

items.question: What is the maximum ITT during the OEI 2.5-minute rating?
items.explanation: The OEI 2.5-minute ITT range is 984°C to 1101°C, with a maximum 2.5-minute value of 1102°C and a 5-second transient limit of 1105°C.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Inter Turbine Temperature (ITT°C), OEI

items.question: What is the normal operating range for engine oil pressure?
items.explanation: Normal engine oil pressure operating range is 2.2 to 6.9 bar.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Oil Pressure (Eng Oil Bar)

items.question: What is the engine starter duty cycle?
options: 45 seconds on, 1 minute off — three times, then 45 seconds on, 30 minutes off
items.explanation: The starter duty cycle is 45 seconds on / 1 minute off, repeated three times, then 45 seconds on followed by 30 minutes off.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Starter Duty Cycle

items.question: What is the maximum continuous main gearbox (MGB) oil temperature?
items.explanation: Maximum normal operation MGB oil temperature is 115°C.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Transmissions Limitations, Oil Temperature

items.question: What is the maximum normal operation intermediate gearbox (IGB) oil temperature?
items.explanation: Maximum normal operation IGB oil temperature is 120°C, slightly higher than the MGB and TGB limit of 115°C.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Transmissions Limitations, Oil Temperature

items.question: What is the normal operation MGB oil pressure range?
items.explanation: Normal MGB oil pressure operating range is 3.1 to 6.0 bar; the idle range is 2.3 to 3.0 bar.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Transmissions Limitations, Oil Pressure

items.question: In powered flight (power-on), what is the maximum continuous rotor speed (NR)?
items.explanation: Power-on maximum continuous NR is 104%, with a 10-second transient limit of 105%.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Rotor Speed Limitations, Power-On

items.question: In autorotation (power-off), what is the maximum continuous rotor speed?
items.explanation: Power-off continuous operation range is 95–110% NR, with a maximum transient of 113%.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Rotor Speed Limitations, Power-Off

items.question: What APU powers the AW189?
items.explanation: The AW189 APU is a Safran Microturbo e-APU 60.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — APU Limitations

items.question: What is the APU starter duty cycle?
options: 10 seconds between attempts, no aborted-start limit
20 seconds delay between attempted starts, 20 minutes delay after 3 aborted starts
No limitation for the APU starter
items.explanation: The APU requires 20 seconds between attempted starts, and 20 minutes after 3 aborted starts (twice through this cycle requires a 40-minute cooldown and troubleshooting).
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — APU Starter Duty Cycle

items.question: What is the normal operating range for engine fuel pressure?
items.explanation: Normal engine fuel pressure operating range is 0.3 to 1.8 bar; the maximum is 1.8 bar.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Fuel System Limitations, Engine Fuel Pressure

items.question: What is the total usable fuel capacity of the AW189?
items.explanation: Total usable fuel capacity is 1320 litres; total unusable fuel is 24 litres.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Fuel System Limitations, Fuel Capacities

items.question: Sideways or crosswind hovering with sustained roll angles greater than ±15° is prohibited when fuel indication, in either tank, is below what value?
items.explanation: Hovering in crosswinds or sideways flight with sustained roll angles greater than ±15° is prohibited when fuel indication in either tank is below 50 kg.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Unusable Fuel

items.question: What is the maximum normal operating hydraulic fluid temperature permitted for takeoff?
items.explanation: Maximum hydraulic fluid temperature permitted for takeoff is 119°C, even though the cautionary range extends to 134°C.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Hydraulics System Limitations, Fluid Temperature

items.question: What is the normal operating range for hydraulic fluid pressure?
items.explanation: Normal hydraulic fluid pressure operating range is 180 to 225 bar; maximum cautionary is 250 bar.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Hydraulics System Limitations, Fluid Pressure

items.question: What is the electrical hydraulic pump used for?
items.explanation: The electrical hydraulic pump is for ground operation only.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Hydraulics System Limitations, Electrical Hydraulic Pump

items.question: What is the maximum rotor speed at which the rotor brake may be applied?
items.explanation: Maximum rotor speed for rotor brake application is 40% NR.
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Rotor Brake Limitations

items.question: What is the maximum AC generator transient load?
items.explanation: AC generator normal operation range is 0–100%, transient range 101–150%, maximum transient 150%. (The APU AC generator's transient limit is slightly higher at 155%.)
references: AW189 RFM Sect. 1 — Electrical System Limitations, AC Generator Load
